keywords.name: Shrapnel
text: Shrapnel is a passive weapon status.

Upon hitting an enemy with a bullet, Shrapnel deals +60% Attack as Weapon DMG to a different random part. The element type is the same as the weapon's element. Addition damage can cause crit damage, hit weakspots, and will decay with distance.

keywords.name: Frost Vortex
text: Frost Vortex is a passive weapon status which causes ice damage to enemies.

Frost Vortex traps enemies within a 4.5m radius and inflicts 50% PSI intensity status damage every 0.5s for 4s. Only 1 Frost Vortex may exist at any time. Addition damage is Frost element damage, it cannot cause crit damage, cannot strike enemy weakspots, and will not decay with distance.

keywords.name: Power Surge
text: Mods with the Power Surge status effect afflict electrical damage to enemies.

keywords.name: Burn
text: Burn is a passive weapon status which causes fire damage to enemies.
Burn deals 12% PSI Intensity as Status DMG every 0.5s for 6s. It can stack up to 5 times.

keywords.name: Unstable Bomber
text: Unstable Bomber is a passive weapon status.

Unstalbe Bomber, once trigger, triggers 1 Status DMG blast of 120 PSI Intensity after 0.1s with a blast radius of 1.5m. The damage decays over the explosion distance, down to a minimum of 50%. Additional damage is Blast damage, it cannot cause crit damage, cannot strike enemy weakspots, and will not decay with distance.

keywords.name: Bounce
text: Bounce is a passive weapon status which causes bullets to ricochet off the target and hit other enemies. If there are no other enemies, the bullet will hit the original target again.

Bounce hits random enemies within 15m radius, then bounces again; each bounce deals DMG equal to 40% of Weapon DMG. If no target is available, bounce to the environment. This effect is non-element. The addition damage can cause crit damage, hit weakspots, and will decay with distance.

keywords.name: Fast Gunner
text: Fast Gunner is a passive weapon status.
While Fast Gunner is in effect, each stack grants Fire Rate +1% and Attack +1% for 2s. Effect can stack up to 5 times.

keywords.name: Fortress Warfare
text: Fortress Warfare is a passive weapon status.
Fortresss Warfare, when triggered, creates an area of effect within a 2m radius that grants allies Heavy Armor for 5s.

keywords.name: The Bull's Eye
text: The Bull's Eye is a passive status effect on specific weapons.
The Bull's Eye marks and highlights a target, increasing their Vulnerability by 8%, lasting 12 seconds.

places.name: LEA Research Lab

places.name: Securement Silo - ALPHA
places.quote: The corrupting influence of a nearby Monolith has infected this old missile silo, transforming it into a nest of Deviants. Rosetta's Securement Squad has recently succeeded in wiping out the Deviants. Now, it's time to wipe out the Securement Squad.
summary: Securement Silo - ALPHA is a mid-level dungeon.

places.name: Securement Silo - PHI

To clear the Seepage Zone you only need to kill the elite Deviant in the middle of the room, you do not need to kill all Deviants.
Avoid stepping on the black liquid on the floor as this causes Sanity to drop.

places.name: Securement Silo - PSI
places.quote: The once prosperous Floeside Salt Mine collapsed in on itself in the aftermath of Starfall. The crack squad of Rosetta troops now stationed inside are left endlessly chasing shadows in pursuit of the dark power that lurks within its frigid depths.
summary: Securement Silo - PSI is a high-level dungeon.
tips: Most rooms in this Silo can be cleared using a high-powered sniper rifle.
To access the hidden room in the "laser traps" area, look for a metal door with a large yellow explosion symbol painted on it and hit it with an explosive (Grenade, Explosives, etc.)

places.name: Securement Silo - SIGMA

For a chance to capture Mr. Wish enter the V3 "keycard room", Mr. Wish is a loot reward for completing the Wish Machine event found within in the Seepage Zone. The loot rate for this Deviation is extremely low/rare, and sometimes it takes hours/days of grinding before Mr. Wish appears as loot.

places.name: Securement Silo - THETA

summary: Securement Silo - THETA is a high-level dungeon.
For a chance to capture Enchanting Void solve the "mirror statues" puzzle and defeat the elite Deviant that appears.
tips: Avoid, as much as possible, standing in the black water as it consumes Sanity.
Having the Bounce stat effect on a weapon will greatly help in the final boss fight as Saint El continuously spawns enemies around himself.

places.name: Prime War
summary: The Prime War (often shortened to "Prime War") is a multiplayer event found within the Manibus and Manibus (Novice) servers in which multiple Meta-Humans gather to defeat a Manibus controlled Boss.
tips: Build defenses near the Staroid Restrainer, as the Boss and their minions are going to damage it.
The Boss spawns from a Silver Puddle, usually located near roads. Some Metas can place foundations around the puddle to distract the boss upon its spawn.
To get 300 points, you can join a Prime War on low health and heal yourself when the event starts.
To get materials for a Gatling Cannon fast, build one in your home and then dismantle it, the materials needed will be transferred into your inventory.
To unlock the next Prime War difficulty, get the highest reward chest - 800, and open it to unlock the next difficulty.

places.quote: Arachsiam the weaver and nurturer of the heterospace, it weaves its own huge cobwebs and spawns countless offspring. Those offenders who break into its territory will become bait for breeding offspring.

This Rift Space was activated in [REDACTED]19 using a Stardust equivalent of approximately 275,400 units. The Rift Space comprises a vast rock cavern containing human structures of unknown age and origin. There is a spatio-temporal connection between the Rift and the Old Hospital that transcends that laws of physics. It is not yet clear why such a connection exists.Deleted Data.

Shoot venom from the abdominal sac
Lunge into the air and slam down upon distant players
Lunge towards players slashing it's sharp forelimbs
Attack close players with its sharp forelimbs.
Spit cobweb: Spit cobwebs to attack the players. The cobwebs will act as traps on the ground, and players will be bound for a few seconds if they step into the traps.
Poison Mist Dispersion: Quickly move to some specific locations and spray poison mist. Players need to hide behind cover to avoid being hurt.
Nurturing larvae: Summons spider eggs in the scene, and the spider eggs will continuously produce self-exploding spiders to quickly approach players.

Mist: Climb up the stone pillar and release the full screen fog, then enter the injury-free state. At the same time, there will be multiple spider eggs constantly producing small spiders in the scene. players can break its injury-free state, only by breaking all the spider eggs.

In its yellow-brown gelatinous appearance, the remains of the devoured soldier could still be seen vaguely. In addition to humans, the weapons that were swallowed together became the tools it used to kill.

Melee Attack: The Foul Shadowhunter's left arm is a sharp claw that can slash and harvest nearby life.

Glue spray: The glue in the body can be sprayed from its head to the surroundings, which will remain on the ground, causing damage and reducing the movement speed and damage reduction rate of the player characters
Jumping Raid: Foul Shadowhunter speeds ​​up and then takes off, using the claw of left arm to hit the ground hard to cause area damage.
Fire coverage: It aims the bazooka on the right hand slowly at the sky, and then continuously shoots. Then multiple missiles are sent out to track the player.
Phase Movement: Flash to the back of the scene, during this period it is invincible.
Summoning: Unleash the aberrations imprisoned in its body, to attack the player.

Melee Attack: Will occasionally swoop toward the Player.
Stalking Attacks: Summons rain clouds and tornadoes, which will follow the Player.
Shadow Corrosion: Shadows from the Black Sector will gradually corrode living organisms. At 10 stacks, HP and Sanity will rapidly deplete.
Black Tornado: Generates a tornado which will follow the Player.
Crystal Projectiles: Throws three crystal projectiles, which will explode into larger crystals upon hitting the ground.
Lightening Strikes: Summons lightening, which will be marked by red AoE areas.
Acid Rain: Generates an acid rain cloud which will follow the Player.

places.name: Shadow Hound
summary: Shadow Hound is the hunter lurking in the shadows, and also the loyal servants of powerful but unknown beings. Shadow Hound is accustomed to live in darkness, leaping out of the shadows to devour its prey.
attacks: Ranged Attack: Breathe out a shadow ball from the mouth, attacking the target at a distance
Melee Attack: Claw and Bite
Shadow Sneak: Sneak into the ground to move in the form of shadows, and then rush out from the ground to attack players.
Black hole: A black hole is generated from its mouth, and the energy will be released when the black hole is fully formed, causing a large-scale explosion.
Shadow Torrent: A torrent formed by ejecting dark matter from its mouth, sweeping the front fan-shaped area and causing damage.
Dark Servant: Summons spherical dark matter to attack the player, and also create a shield to protect itself.

Oblivion: Jump into the air and rotate at high speed to form a shadow meteorite with huge energy. After forming, it smashes to the ground, causing high area damage. When Shadow Hound begins to form a shadow meteorite in the sky, the skill can be interrupted if players concentrate fire.

Tangled Vines: Summons 3 Tangled Vines from the ground to attack the player, at the same time Treant is in an immune state until the summoned Vines are destroyed.
"Mother"'s Wailing: Treant opens its back, revealing the bound woman, who will wail in pain and causing damage to surrounding players.
Piercing Thorns: Generate huge thorns under the player's feet, dealing damage

places.name: Calamity Tower
parts: The fight

From solo challenges that progress with the main story, to team battles, and then to the abyss challenge in Phase II, the Calamity Tower will progressively test your ship cannon handling, ship maneuvering, and cooperate skills.
Combat revolves around tentacles and weakspots: clear outer threats and seize the moment when weakspots are exposed to focus fire.
Some tentacles are protected by building protection, and the destructive power of ship cannons will come into play here.
In Phase II, after completing the prerequisite challenges, you can venture deeper into Calamity Tower: Abyss.
Rewards
Completing challenges in the main story will advance the unlock of corresponding gear craft.
consume Heart of the Ocean during the reward stage of Calamity Tower or the Sunken Lord to obtain the scenario's new Mods

the marked Meta becomes the enemy's pursuit target while also gaining a key opportunity to attack the alpha.
Pick up fallen feathers to gain a brief lift-off ability, touch the floating energy orbs to counter the Calamity Owl, and seize an advantage for the battles ahead.

places.name: Sea Calamity Zone (Calamity Hatchling)
parts: The fight

In Phase II's waters, a Calamity Zone will appear. The central Calamity Hatchling is surrounded by deviated turrets, naval mines, and enemies, testing ship configuration and naval combat capabilities.

Use ship cannons to blast open buildings, detonate naval mines early to clear routes, or destroy turret support structures to break their firepower. Then destroy the shield core in the outer buildings to remove the central shield, and defeat the Calamity Hatchling for rewards.

places.name: The Sunken Lord
parts: When it opens
When the server's purification progress reaches 100%, the Sunken Lord's entrance platform will rise from underwater.
The fight
Metas must work together to defeat the Calamity Hatchling in the entrance area, complete the door battle, then team up to go deeper and challenge the Sunken Lord's Core.
From tentacle sieges and arrayed barrage to violent smashes with a battered hull, the spreading slime and illusions will also compress safe space.
Rewards
Challenge The Sunken Lord for a chance to obtain the new Deviation "Duet".
Challenge the Sunken Lord, or consume Heart of the Ocean during the reward stage of Calamity Tower or the Sunken Lord to obtain the scenario's new Mods

places.name: Drifting Greenhouse
parts: The fight

In Phase II's waters, drifting greenhouses will appear on specific islands. After Metas approach the island, the drifting greenhouse will summon poison pools while flying up from them. Metas need to weave through the poison pools to dodge and defeat the greenhouse.
Rewards
After defeating the greenhouse, in addition to dropping rewards, deviated plants will refresh on the field. You can gather these plants to obtain bonus rewards.

sections.title: Coming back after a break
sections.intro: The game you left is not the game you load into. Levels no longer gate gear, Memetics became the Tech tree, and the newest scenario is at sea. Read the changes below, then follow the steps.

paras.t: April 8, 2026 (v2.3.6): the Tech tree was rebuilt around four branches: Survival, Production, Combat and Building. You unlock Tech by reverse engineering, by invention at the Synthesis Bench, or by spending Tech Points. The old Specialization system was removed.

Same patch: gear has no level requirement any more, the starting weapon is the [[Rustic Crossbow]], tiered materials were merged (one Fabric, one Parts, one Plastic), and tin and aluminum ore no longer spawn.
Calibration blueprints are added during crafting at the Advanced Supplies Workbench: on the crafting screen, the square marked "Optional" under "Crafting Materials" opens them.
September 2026: classes matter. A Beastmaster can summon 3 animals at once, every other class 1. Only a Beastmaster gets an animal's active and passive skills while riding.
September 16, 2026: [[MG4 - Conflicting Memories]] was reworked to trigger Shrapnel every 6 hits, and the [[Treacherous Tides Set]] now scales with HP instead of Sanity.
October 21, 2026 (v3.1.1): the ocean scenario Isles of Abyss launched, with two new Frost Vortex pieces, [[o:SOCR - Cosmic Visitor]] and the [[o:Snowline Elite Vest]].

November 18, 2026 (v3.2.1): the Visional Wheel S5: Dissonant Resonance season opened, the [[Bastille Set]] was reworked, the [[o:Tactical Combat Boots]] effect changed, and a new Deviation, [[o:Silent Statue O-079]], was added.

steps.t: Open your mail.
Claim the November 18 maintenance rewards: Starchrom ×1,000 and Mitsuko's Mark ×100.
Open the scenario selection screen.
If you want the newest content, sign up for Isles of Abyss: your Blueprints and Mods come with you.
Open the Blueprint System.
Spend Starchrom on the blueprint of the one weapon your build needs (see Builds).
Pick one damage keyword for your build (see Builds).
Fit a weapon, armor set, mods and Deviation that all feed that keyword.
If a guide you find tells you to spend Specialization points, skip that guide: that system was removed in v2.3.6.
If you wear Bastille pieces from an older build, re-read the [[Bastille Set]] effect in game: it was reworked on November 18 and the wiki text still shows the old version.

sections.check: Check: your weapon card shows the keyword you picked, and your gear screen has no level lock.

sections.title: Words the guide uses
sections.intro: Short meanings for the game's own words. Each line cites where it comes from.

terms.t: What the game calls players: Meta-Humans, a new type of human created by Rosetta. The official notes address you as Metas.
A Visional Wheel season runs on separate Vision servers (VisionWorld #) next to the normal ones. You travel there through a Worldstone.
The teleport point you use to switch to another world, including the Vision world.
A system other scenarios have, with bonuses (Cradle Overrides) that builds can lean on. Isles of Abyss has no Cradle.
On a PvP server, a territory running Territory Purification enters the Chaotic State, and other players can attack it.
A material from missions, Public Crisis Events, dungeons and Warband Activities. Purify it in a Stardust Filter at your territory for Stardust Source while Deviants attack.
The Isles of Abyss advanced resource. Spend it at the reward stage of challenges such as the Calamity Tower and the Sunken Lord.
An Isles of Abyss region with its own harsh weather; bring that zone's counter item (see the table on Isles of Abyss).
The progression tree that replaced Memetics in v2.3.6, with four branches: Survival, Production, Combat and Building.
The effect a weapon triggers (Shrapnel, Frost Vortex, Power Surge and so on). Your mods, set and Deviation should feed it.
A basic currency. You spend it to enhance weapon and armor blueprints in the Blueprint System. Its monthly cap is on Daily and weekly.
An armor stat. Blueprint tiers raise an armor piece's HP, Pollution Resist and Psi Intensity. MMO Culture notes that vortex damage scales with Psi Intensity.
A meter you lose in some areas, for example Black Tide areas in Isles of Abyss. Low Sanity cuts your Max HP. A Sanity Gummy gives +60 Sanity.
The gameplay theme of a server, for example Manibus, Endless Dream, Prismverse's Clash, RaidZone or Isles of Abyss. Each scenario runs for a season, and a season is split into phases.

A progress meter shared by the whole server in Isles of Abyss. As it advances, Phase I gets shorter, and at 100% the Sunken Lord's entrance platform rises from underwater. The official notes do not say what raises it.

A different thing: an event at your own territory. Build a Stardust Resonant Filter, spend Eclipse Cortexes (PvE) or Chaotic Cortexes (PvP), and defend the filter from waves of enemies. It is one of the main ways to earn Stardust. The wiki page is from 2024.

Isles of Abyss names for its big challenges: the Calamity Tower (solo and team challenges, with Calamity Tower: Abyss in Phase II), the Calamity Nest (a land stronghold where the Calamity Owl fights you) and the Sea Calamity Zone (Phase II waters, around the Calamity Hatchling).
One of the Haywire Zone phenomena in Isles of Abyss. It drains Sanity. The Black Tide Protective Mask slows the Sanity loss, but it uses up Durability while it is on.
A private sandbox island for your character, separate from your current Scenario. Building there uses only Astral Sand, which you get by selling items in its Island Shop.
Mods handed out as event and Visional Redemption rewards. The cached sources do not say how they differ from normal mods.
Tokens for the Lightforge Loot Crate, the game's paid gacha. The Advanced Edition Battle Pass and the Visional Redemption Shop also give them.
An S5 item from Resonance Boxes. You trade it at Event - Visional Redemption - Redeem Shop for Lightforge Ingots, Shiny Mods, Deviations and cosmetics.
A currency for the Challenge Shop. Scenario challenges, Journey tasks and the weekly Paradise Challenge (100 a week) give it.
The game's big bosses: powerful beings that do not belong to the human world. Their cards are under Bosses and dungeons.
Points you spend to unlock Tech. You earn them by leveling up, repeating research and defeating Elite enemies. Since v2.3.6 Mystical Crates no longer give them.
The S5 currency. Resonant Movements, The Echo War and the Visional Wheel event give it, and you spend it on Resonance tiers and Echoes into Verses rewards.

Enemy ships in Isles of Abyss. Sail your ship into battle against them, destroy their key facilities, board their decks and loot their holds. They get stronger as your voyage goes on, and larger Voyager Fleets appear after Phase II.

The main game mode of the current Vision: four kinds of areas (Movement of Delight, Wrath, Lament and Terror) appear across Nalcott. Use your reticle to pick up notes and put the melody back in order.
A weekly event in the current Vision. Challenge each region of Resonant Movements to build Active Progress for rewards such as Weapon Skins and Lightforge Ingots.
The Journey menu's Commissions tab has 4 Commission Boards of weekly tasks. They unlock once a week, and each board has 6 free refreshes.

The style name on a weapon or armor card. Each armor set has a style linked to the game's organizations: Beyonder, Juggernaut and Operator to Rosetta and The Union, Huntsman to Mayflys, Stranger to Vultures, Wanderer to Mayflys and Vultures. The cached wiki pages do not say that a style changes stats.

A finished weapon or armor piece found as loot (weapon crates, hoarder's pouches, armor and gear crates) instead of crafted from a blueprint. Disassembling some Dropped Gear weapons gives a calibration blueprint.
The Build Mode facility in your territory that holds a captured Deviation. Its old name is Isolated Securement Unit.
A refined material that contains Stardust energy. Its main use is calibrating weapons and armor at the Gear Workbench. It also goes into Quick Activators and Adrenaline Shots.

sections.title: About Isles of Abyss, the current scenario
sections.intro: A PvE ocean scenario on a cycle of about 21 days: Phase I, then Phase II, then a rest stage. You start at max level and grow through Tech, not levels.

paras.t: Phase I lasts about 5 to 10 days and gets shorter as the server's purification progress rises. Phase II lasts 11 days and unlocks the endgame fight, [[o:The Sunken Lord]].
Each server has 12 worlds.
Characters start at max level. Tech decides what rarity of gear you can craft, and how many Mod attributes are active. The Cradle is not available here.
Your ship is both your vehicle and a movable water territory. Build it in Build Mode; after that, place it with Relocation or the summon vehicle key.
Heart of the Ocean is the scenario's advanced resource: you spend it at the reward stage of challenges such as the Calamity Tower and the Sunken Lord to open Mod and collection rewards.
Since November 18 the world map shows a countdown to the next phase once the current phase's progress is full.

sections.title: How to progress through Isles of Abyss
sections.need: You'll need: a character signed up for Isles of Abyss. Phase I can end in 5 days (this guide's reading: start early).

steps.t: Gather basic supplies along the coast of Fragrant Cape.
Search the grounded shipwrecks for materials.
Build your first ship in Build Mode (key B).
Save the ship design so you can place it again quickly.
Put on the Basic Diving Suit.
Apply Fish Oil Paste before your first dive.
Bring the counter item for the Haywire Zone you are sailing to (see the table on Isles of Abyss).
Clear the solo Calamity Tower challenges in the main story: they unlock the matching gear crafting.
Collect Heart of the Ocean from Voyagers, journey objectives and the crates you find.
Help raise the server's purification progress: it shortens Phase I and opens the Sunken Lord.
In Phase II, take on Calamity Tower: Abyss, the Sea Calamity Zone and the Drifting Greenhouse.
In Phase II, unlock the Phase II cannons.
Spend Heart of the Ocean at the reward stage of the Calamity Tower or the Sunken Lord to roll for the scenario's new Mods, Precision Load and Turret Enhancement.

sections.check: Check: when Phase I progress is full, the world map shows a countdown to Phase II.

sections.title: How to build and arm a ship
sections.need: You'll need: wood or metal for hull parts and at least one cannon unlocked in Tech.

steps.t: Press B to open Build Mode.
Choose a new water vessel.
Lay the hull from square, triangular, sloped and curved parts.
Add the deck, gunwale, bow and handrails.
Fit a propulsion system (tiers from lowest to highest: manual, sail, fuel, electric drive).
If the ship turns too slowly, add Boosters or side-thruster steering gear.
Mount cannons that match your target (see the cannon table).
Select the structures connected to the core deck.
Save the ship design.
While sailing, switch between cannons with the Wheel.
To stop, slow down below 14 km/h.
Drop the anchor: Spacebar on PC, X on console.
If a big squid grabs the ship, shoot its tentacles off: it flees once they are severed.

sections.check: Check: the summon vehicle key places your saved ship next to you.

sections.title: How to beat the Isles of Abyss bosses
sections.intro: All five fights below come from the official scenario notes. The fan wiki has no pages for them yet, so there are no numbers beyond what the developers published.

steps.t: Calamity Tower: kill the support tentacles first (they heal, share damage or summon).
Calamity Tower: focus fire on the weakspot when it opens.
Calamity Tower: if a tentacle has building protection, hit it with cannons.
Calamity Nest (Calamity Owl): protect the teammate marked by Revenge; that player is chased but also gets the best chance to hit the boss.
Calamity Nest on higher difficulty: pick up fallen feathers to lift off.
Calamity Nest on higher difficulty: touch the floating energy orbs to counter the owl.
Sea Calamity Zone: blow up the naval mines early.
Sea Calamity Zone: destroy the turret supports.
Sea Calamity Zone: break the shield core in the outer buildings.
Sea Calamity Zone: kill the Calamity Hatchling.
Drifting Greenhouse: weave between the poison pools to reach the greenhouse.
Drifting Greenhouse: kill the greenhouse.
Drifting Greenhouse: gather the deviated plants it leaves for bonus rewards.
The Sunken Lord (purification at 100%): kill the Calamity Hatchling at the entrance.
The Sunken Lord: win the door battle.
The Sunken Lord: push through the corridors to the core while lava shrinks the safe space.

sections.check: Check: when you beat the Sunken Lord or a Calamity Tower challenge, its reward stage opens, where you can spend Heart of the Ocean. The official notes name a reward stage only for these two.
sections.tip: Tip: the Sunken Lord can drop the new Deviation Duet.

sections.title: How to play Season 5: Dissonant Resonance
sections.intro: A Vision season that opened with v3.2.1 on November 18, 2026. Reach it through the Worldstone. It runs in Isles of Abyss, Manibus (not the Novice Scenario) and five more scenarios.

steps.t: Go to a Worldstone.
Switch to the Vision world.
Find a Movement area on the map: Delight, Wrath, Lament or Terror. Each has its own difficulty.
Ring the Echo Bell to start the Movement. You get your untuned score.
Kill the Dissonant Army enemies that carry notes.
Shoot the notes your score asks for, in order, before they vanish.
Kill the Dissonant Emissary at the end. If your own score is full you get a Legendary Movement; if not, a smaller reward.
From 15 minutes into the Vision, enter The Echo War through the portal on the map: up to 4 players, Basic or Hard.
In The Echo War, deal with the summoned minions first.
When the weak point opens, focus fire on it.
Spend Divine Rhythm in the Redeem Shop (Event - Visional Redemption) on Lightforge Ingots, Shiny Mods or top Deviations.

sections.check: Check: after the Dissonant Emissary dies, your reward shows a Legendary Movement if your own score was full.
sections.tip: Tip (this guide's reading): Dissonant Dust has a weekly cap. Past it the drop rate falls, so spread your farming across the week.

sections.title: About season phases and what resets

paras.t: A season is split into phases; each phase unlocks regions, features and difficulty levels. The number of phases depends on the scenario.

Mandatory season wipes were removed in 2025: you can sign a character up for a permanent server during the settlement phase. Permanent servers for PvP scenarios were discontinued on December 10, 2025.
When a season closes, these do not carry over: character level experience, map exploration progress, scenario core gameplay items, and special items made with tech enhancement.
Eligible items go to Transit Storage, and your territory is saved as a Territory or Vehicle Blueprint Backup you can rebuild from Build Mode.
Isles of Abyss: your Blueprints and Mods come with you; the Cradle is not available; after both phases a rest stage begins.

Isles of Abyss: a permanent server opens before the first servers close, so everyone can merge into it. The October 16 dev blog expected it on November 12; the October 21 update notes say November 18. No cached post confirms the opening yet.

Starchrom is capped per month, and the cap opens in steps through the month. The sources disagree on the size: the wiki page (edited September 2026) says 30,000; Timesaver (November 14, 2026) says 66,000, opening on the 1st, 8th, 15th and 22nd. The Blueprint screen shows your live cap.

sections.title: How to use your daily and weekly play time
sections.intro: Every day, claim your Battle Pass crate chances. Every week, clear the Commission Boards, the Dissonant Dust cap, Movement Rotation and the Paradise Challenge. Through the month, open saved Starchrom crates as the cap steps up.

steps.t: Every day after 6:00 server time: open the Battle Pass screen.
Claim a Rare Stardust Secret Crate for every 300 Battle Pass Exp while you have chances left (2 a day Monday to Thursday, 4 a day Friday to Sunday; they stack up to 20).
Every day: if a limited-time event on the Events screen has a daily check-in, do it.
Every week: open the Commissions tab of the Journey screen (J).
Complete the Commission Boards that unlocked this week; each board has 6 free refreshes for tasks you do not want.
Every week: farm Dissonant Dust in Resonant Movements and The Echo War until the weekly cap.
Every week: clear every region's Resonant Movements for the Movement Rotation event (Weapon Skins and Lightforge Ingots).
Every week: finish the Paradise Challenge in Eternaland for its weekly 100 Mitsuko's Mark.
If you run Territory Purification, plan on the wiki's limit of 40 Cortexes per week with a Monday reset. That page was last edited in 2024 and is not confirmed since v2.3.6.
On the 1st, 8th, 15th and 22nd of the month, open the Active Starchrom Crates you saved: per Timesaver, that is when the next part of the monthly Starchrom cap unlocks.
Each month: work through the monthly challenge on the Scenario Challenge tab for Mitsuko's Marks.
Each update: claim the maintenance mail before it expires after 28 days.
Isles of Abyss, Phase I: push the server's purification progress.
Isles of Abyss, Phase II: run Calamity Tower: Abyss and the Sunken Lord for their rewards.

sections.title: About damage keywords
sections.intro: Most guns carry one damage keyword (Shrapnel, Frost Vortex, Power Surge, Burn, Unstable Bomber, Bounce, Fast Gunner, Fortress Warfare or The Bull's Eye). In this guide's weapon cards, melee weapons, B.P. weapons and some plain guns have none, and [[AUG - Electron Cloud]] and [[R500 - Hammerhead Shark]] carry two. MMO Culture calls the keyword a build's damage engine: everything else in a build is there to trigger it more often or make it hit harder. Each keyword card below lists every weapon, mod and set in the data that names it.

paras.t: Your mods, armor set and Deviation should either make the keyword trigger more often or make it hit harder. A piece that does neither is a wasted slot.
Most builds use a second gun (a sniper or hand cannon) only to apply [[The Bull's Eye]] mark before switching to the main weapon.

sections.title: How to put a build together
sections.need: You'll need: the blueprint of a keyword weapon and four pieces of one armor set.

steps.t: Pick the keyword you want from the Builds page.
Craft the anchor weapon for that keyword, with the calibration blueprint you want added during crafting.
Put a weapon mod on it that boosts that keyword, not a generic stat.
Wear four pieces of the build's armor set.
Fill the other armor slots with the pieces the build lists on the Builds page.
Put a gear mod in every armor slot that feeds the same keyword.
Take the combat Deviation the build names.
Eat a combat dish before every boss.
If you keep dying with Shrapnel, switch to Frost Vortex: both sources call it the safer solo pick.

sections.check: Check: every piece in your loadout mentions your keyword, crit (for Shrapnel and Unstable Bomber) or the element (for Frost Vortex, Power Surge and Burn).

sections.title: How to craft a weapon with a calibration blueprint
sections.need: You'll need: the weapon's blueprint, its materials, and an Advanced Supplies Workbench.

steps.t: Disassemble a Dropped Gear weapon that shows the light-blue document-and-arrow icon to get its calibration blueprint.
Open the backpack (I).
Look at the blueprint under Tools: the percentages next to each stat show its range.
Open the weapon's recipe at the Advanced Supplies Workbench.
Click the blinking Optional square under Crafting Materials.
Pick the calibration blueprint.
Craft the weapon.

sections.check: Check: the crafted weapon's card shows the calibration stats.
sections.tip: Tip: calibration blueprints do not exist in Deviation: Survive, Capture, Preserve.

sections.title: How to spend Tech (the system that replaced Memetics)
sections.intro: Tech replaced Memetics and level-gated unlocks in v2.3.6. The official notes give no order. The steps below are a suggested order: this guide's reading of the notes, not an official one.

steps.t: Pick up items and facilities marked as cultural artifacts while exploring.
Reverse engineer them at the Synthesis Bench: this can unlock a recipe or give Tech Points directly.
Read books you find in scrap: they give Tech Points.
Unlock the advanced crafting facilities first, such as the Enhanced Supplies Workbench: the intermediate benches were removed and their recipes moved into the advanced ones.
Raise your Tech level to raise the generator limit from 6 to 8.
Before you spend an enhancement point, read what it unlocks: enhancement results are fixed and cannot be reset.
If you are short on points, kill Elite enemies; Mystical Crates no longer give Tech Points.

sections.check: Check: the Tech node you picked shows as unlocked on the Tech screen.
sections.tip: Tip (this guide's reading): in Isles of Abyss, your Tech progress limits the gear rarity you can craft and how many Mod attributes are active, so push Tech before gear.

sections.title: How to catch and use a Deviation
sections.need: You'll need: good gloves (Deviation Capture rises with glove tier and repair).

steps.t: Look up where the Deviation spawns on its card (Deviations page).
If it does not spawn in your world, switch worlds at a Worldstone; your territory stays where it is.
Face the floating orb.
Press F to start the capture.
Put a Combat Deviation in a Securement Pod.
Press Synchronize to carry it.
In Deviation: Survive, Capture, Preserve, use Binding Grenades instead: they are the only way to capture there, and you command three Deviations.

sections.check: Check: your backpack's Deviation tab holds up to 96; extra captures arrive by mail.
sections.tip: Tip: the wiki's spawn lists cover the older scenarios, not Isles of Abyss. There, the official notes name the activity instead, for example Calamity Tower or Voyagers for the new Morphed Deviations; those cards show it first.

sections.title: How to set up a base (territory)
sections.need: You'll need: a Territory Core and building materials in storage or your backpack.

steps.t: Pick a spot away from other territories, away from settlement enemy spawns, and outside Pollution Zones.
Place the Territory Core to mark out the area.
Press B for Build Mode.
Place structures inside the area; the default limits are 300 Structures and 100 Facilities and Furniture.
Build the crafting facilities you need (see Facilities).
Build a [[Stardust Resonant Filter]] (Facilities, 4th tab, Function Facility).
Put defenses around the filter: the enemies run at it.
Run Territory Purification with Eclipse Cortexes to earn Stardust Source and Starchrom.
If you need to move, open Build Mode at the new spot.
Press Z (Territory Relocation).

sections.check: Check: the Territory Core's area shows on the ground, and Build Mode lets you place structures inside it.
sections.tip: Tip: on a PvP server, Purification puts your territory in the Chaotic State, so other players can attack it.

sections.title: How to run a Securement Silo
sections.need: You'll need: Hard or higher for Legendary mods from SIGMA and PHI (the other Silos can drop Legendary on Normal). Each Silo drops one armor mod slot (see the Silo card).

steps.t: Pick the Silo whose mod slot you need from Bosses and dungeons (for example EX1 drops Mask mods).
Talk to T-Man outside the Silo for the Bounty task.
Choose Hard or higher if you want Legendary mods: on Normal some Silos cap lower.
Kill the boss.
Get the access card from the control room.
Open the depot with the access card.
If the Deviation did not drop, run the Silo again: a capture is possible but not guaranteed.

sections.check: Check: the depot opens and its loot shows the mod for that Silo's slot.
sections.tip: Tip: in PHI, keep out of the black liquid; it drains Sanity.

not_carded.t: Memetics and Memetic Specialization pages: they describe the system v2.3.6 (April 2026) replaced with Tech, so there are no Memetics cards; the Tech page follows the official notes. Facilities on those pages that still exist have facility cards.
Monoliths (Forsaken Monolith, Mirage Monolith, Monolith of Greed): no cards.
Ordinary enemies and some world bosses, for example Hell Hound (which a weapon card names as a drop source): no cards. Boss cards cover the Great Ones, the Isles of Abyss bosses and two world bosses.

tiers.title: Build tier list
tiers.what: These letters are relayed, not first-hand. raidrig says its tiers 'come from community tier lists'; Gamespec quotes 'one recent list' without naming it. Both may be passing on the same list, so two matching letters can be one rating counted twice. Neither site defines its letters: read S as its top group and each later letter as a lower group. A dash means that site gives no letter.
tiers.answer: Both sites relay Shrapnel and Frost Vortex in S. They split on Power Surge (A or S) and Fast Gunner (B or A). Only Gamespec's relayed list rates Unstable Bomber, Bull's Eye and Burn. Only raidrig's rates Bounce (A).
tiers.relay_note: Whose rating: unnamed community tier lists, relayed by raidrig and Gamespec. This guide adds no letters.
tiers.others: raidrig also relays Bounce and Starfall Inversion in A, but gives no weapon, mods or Deviation for either. The other build sources here give no Starfall Inversion build, so it has no row, and Bounce has no build page.
